topic: JVM Internals (Memory Model, G1/ZGC, Class Loading)

questions.question: What is the primary cause of this `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace` leak?
options: A) Each execution creates a new `GroovyClassLoader` instance which generates new `Class` metadata in Metaspace, and these `Class` objects cannot be GC'd because `GroovyClassLoader` maintains implicit strong references to them.
B) The JVM Heap is too small, causing the heap allocations from `script.run()` to spill over into `Metaspace`.
C) The Spring `@Service` annotation marks this class as a singleton, causing all `scriptSource` strings to be pinned in the JVM String table inside `Metaspace`.
D) The `G1` Garbage Collector does not clean up `Metaspace` dynamically unless `-XX:+ClassUnloadingWithConcurrentMark` is disabled.
questions.correct_answer_text: A) Each execution creates a new `GroovyClassLoader` instance which generates new `Class` metadata in Metaspace, and these `Class` objects cannot be GC'd because `GroovyClassLoader` maintains implicit strong references to them.
questions.explanation: In Java, class metadata resides in `Metaspace`. A `Class` object can only be Garbage Collected if its defining `ClassLoader` is eligible for GC. In this snippet, creating a new `GroovyClassLoader` per execution parses and loads a unique class into `Metaspace`. Unless the `GroovyClassLoader` and all loaded class instances are completely unreferenced and collected, the class metadata stays pinned in `Metaspace`, quickly exhausting memory.

questions.question: What JVM Memory Model mechanism causes threads to read a partially initialized `instance` object?
options: A) Memory access reordering allows the JVM to allocate memory and assign the non-null reference to `instance` before the constructor finishes initializing `configMap`.
B) The `synchronized` block fails to create a happens-before relationship for read operations occurring outside the monitor.
C) The `G1` Garbage Collector relocates `configMap` during concurrent mark phase, causing temporary unaligned reads.
D) Spring context initialization wraps `ConfigurationRegistry` in a CGLIB proxy that breaks single-check volatile reads.
questions.correct_answer_text: A) Memory access reordering allows the JVM to allocate memory and assign the non-null reference to `instance` before the constructor finishes initializing `configMap`.
questions.explanation: Without declaring `instance` as `volatile`, the JVM and CPU are permitted to reorder instructions for performance optimization. Specifically, object memory allocation and assigning the address to `instance` can happen BEFORE the constructor code (initializing `configMap`) executes. Another thread reading `instance` outside the `synchronized` block sees a non-null `instance` pointer and attempts to read `configMap`, which has not yet been initialized. Marking `instance` as `volatile` adds write barriers preventing instruction reordering.

questions.scenario: You are debugging a production issue where a ultra-low-latency financial application migrated from `G1GC` to non-generational `ZGC` (`-XX:+UseZGC`) on Java 17. During peak trading bursts, application threads experience latency spikes of up to 500ms. Garbage Collector logs show frequent messages reading `Allocation Stall`.
questions.question: What is the root cause of these `Allocation Stall` events under `ZGC`, and how should it be resolved?
options: A) The application thread allocation rate exceeds the speed at which `ZGC` reclaims memory, forcing application threads to pause and wait for GC cycle completion.
B) `ZGC` colored pointers exceed the 42-bit virtual memory address space limit, causing kernel-level page fault stalls.
C) `ZGC` does not support parallel thread allocation buffers (TLABs), forcing all object allocations onto a single synchronized heap lock.
D) `ZGC` triggers Stop-The-World root scanning whenever `Metaspace` reaches 80% capacity under peak load.
questions.correct_answer_text: A) The application thread allocation rate exceeds the speed at which `ZGC` reclaims memory, forcing application threads to pause and wait for GC cycle completion.
questions.explanation: An `Allocation Stall` in `ZGC` occurs when application threads allocate memory faster than `ZGC` can concurrently mark and compact garbage. When available heap space runs out before GC finishes a cycle, allocating threads are stalled/paused until memory is freed. Solutions include tuning `-XX:ConcGCThreads` to give GC more CPU cycles, increasing overall max heap size (`-Xmx`), or upgrading to Generational ZGC (Java 21+).
